memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He took the tablets of the covenant law and placed them in the ark, attached the poles to the ark and put the atonement cover over it. Then he brought the ark into the tabernacle and hung the shielding curtain and shielded the ark of the covenant law, as the Lord commanded him." - Exod 40:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The law went into the ark. The atonement cover went over the law. That is the arrangement at the very heart of Israel's worship.

God's commands — which Israel had already broken spectacularly — lay inside a box. Over them sat the place where blood was sprinkled once a year.

The law was not destroyed. It was not softened or rewritten. It was covered.

That is exactly what happens at the cross. Christ did not abolish the law's demands; He satisfied them. God made Him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God (2 Cor 5:21). The record of debt that stood against us was nailed to the cross (Col 2:14).

Sit with the geography of it. Between God's holiness above and God's broken law below stood a covering of mercy. Everything depended on what was in between.

Everything still does.

Notice too that these were the second set of tablets. The first lay shattered at the foot of the mountain. God wrote again — and then covered what He had written with mercy.

If you fear that your record condemns you, look at what sits over it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live as though your record is still exposed before God?
2. What does it mean that the law was covered rather than cancelled?
3. How does this change the way you handle guilt over past sin?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, my broken record lies under Your mercy. Thank You that You satisfied what I could never keep. Amen.
